On The 5 th Of January, 2026
 Misc. Criminal Case No. 58604 of 2025

Mujib Khan
 Versus
 The State Of Madhya Pradesh
 Appearance:
 Shri Paritosh Trivedi - Advocate for applicant.
Shri Yogesh Dhande - Government Advocate for State.

Order 
This is the first application filed by the applicant under Section 482 of BNSS for grant of anticipatory bail apprehending his arrest in connection with Crime No.240/2025 registered at Police Station - Bilkhiriya, District Bhopal (M.P.) for the offence punishable under Sections 420,
467, 468, 471 and 120-B of IPC.

2. As per the prosecution story the allegation against the applicant is that he prepared the forged documents and given the government land to other person by executing a gift deed therefore, the aforesaid offence has been registered against him and co-accused persons.
3. Learned counsel for the applicant submits that applicant is innocent and has been falsely implicated in this case.
It is further submitted that for obtaining the electricity connection, gift deed of land was executed by Mohd. Farukh in favour of present applicant.

It is further submitted that the State NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-JBP:131 2 MCRC-58604-2025 had already taken possession of the land from the present applicant, even then the present case has been registered against the present applicant.
It is further submitted that present applicant had no knowledge that the said land belongs to the State.
He has not made any forged document.
Therefore, it has been prayed that the applicant may be released on bail.

4. On the other hand, learned counsel for State has opposed the grant of bail to the applicant and submitted that the State is the real owner of the land, but Mohd. Farukh has sold the government land to the present applicant and present applicant was well aware of the fact that Mohd. Farukh is not the owner of this land, even then he purchased the government land from Mohd. Farukh.

Hence,
the applicant does not deserve grant of anticipatory bail.

6. Looking to aforesaid facts and circumstances as well as allegation levelled against the applicant and seriousness of offence, I am not inclined to grant anticipatory bail to the present applicant.
7. Accordingly, present MCRC stands dismissed.
